summary: myidsan gains Kerberos SPNEGO single sign-on (Phase 2 of docs/MYIDSAN_ENTERPRISE_SSO_PLAN.md): a domain-joined browser's existing Windows/AD login authenticates it against myidsan with no password prompt. A new pure-Go infra/login/kerberos.go (github.com/jcmturner/gokrb5/v8, pinned v8.4.4) loads an exported service keytab at boot and verifies a request's Authorization: Negotiate token via SPNEGO AcceptSecContext; a missing token yields a 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Negotiate challenge (not an error), while a bad/expired ticket or a realm outside the configured allow-list is a real refusal. The verified principal carries no email/groups by itself, so a new infra/login.LdapLookup (service-bind search, no user bind) and apps/myidsan/services/directory.go's ResolveDirectoryUser resolve it through the same directory and group->role mapping a password/LDAP login for that person would use - one person, one account, regardless of credential path; a directory-less install falls back to a principal-derived standalone identity instead. GET /api/login/kerberos is the new endpoint (apps/myidsan/apis/login.go, NewLoginApi refactored to take a LoginApiOptions struct): success issues the session and redirects to the pending continue target; any failure (rejected ticket, disallowed realm, unresolvable principal) redirects to /api/auth/login?error=sso_failed with an inline message rather than a dead-end 401 page, and is counted in myidsan_federated_login_total{provider="kerberos",result=...} (ticket_rejected, realm_refused, unreachable, not_in_directory, identity_conflict, inactive). apps/myidsan/apis/federated_auth.go renders a configurable-label 'Windows (SSO)' button alongside the existing social/LDAP options. A new kerberos config block (enabled, keytabPath, servicePrincipal, onlyRealms, displayLabel) controls it; apps/myidsan/app/app.go loads the keytab at boot and, on a bad/missing keytab, logs a warning and leaves Kerberos 'not offered' rather than failing startup, mirroring how a half-configured OAuth provider is handled.
compatibility: Backward compatible: kerberos.enabled defaults to false in both apps/myidsan/config.json and config.dev.json, so existing installs see no change in login behavior, no new button, and no 401 challenge on any route until an operator provisions a keytab and opts in. The per-IP login lockout (loginSecurity) is unchanged and does not apply to the new Kerberos route, since a ticket is cryptographically verified rather than guessed. Not yet verified against a real KDC/realm - unit-tested (keytab load, no-token-means-challenge, garbage-token rejection, realm allow-list, standalone identity derivation) and live-booted (challenge/redirect behavior with an unconfigured and a garbage-token request) but the full AcceptSecContext success path needs a domain-joined client and a live KDC, which the user will test separately.
